sections.bodyEn: FS01 chiming movement Created by CW’s technical director Frank Seltzer, Calibre FS01 is an ingenious modified movement with Christopher Ward’s DNA in every cog and spring. With an inspired piece of lateral thinking, Frank realised that CW’s ‘jumping hour’ movement could be adapted to create a chiming sound on the hour, every hour. More than 60 new components form the striking mechanism module which sits atop a Sellita SW200-1 base movement which provides the 38-hour power reserve.
A Globolight® ring and tipped hands for nocturnal accuracy
Sunray-patterned dial printed with Super-LumiNova® for after-dark illumination.
A Globolight® ring and tipped hands for nocturnal accuracy
‘Songbird’ striking hammer hits the steel spring to achieve the ‘beautiful singing’ of the D note
The 41mm Light-catcher™ case is forged from Grade 5 titanium to amplify the sound of the chime

Redesigned and slimmer Light-catcher™ case. NEW Sellita SW200-2 Power+ automatic movement with 65-hour power reserve. NEW conical crown – without guards. Fully polished bezel. Sapphire ‘exhibition’ caseback. NEW polished lacquer dial. Slimmer polished hands. Simpler seconds hand – with non-Trident counterbalance. Diamond-polished and tapered indexes – filled with lume. NEW in-house-designed rotor with skeletonised arm. Raised, applied date window at 6 o’clock. ‘Sealander’ logotype on the dial for the first time. The debut of iLink™, a system that enables tool-free link adjustment on Bader and Consort™ bracelets. Also available on sporty rubber strap with Bader buckle. Available in the NEW warmer White, NEW Pistachio, NEW Pink, Sky Blue plus Black – in both 36mm and 39mm.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.
New conical crown without crown guards
Linear and circular brushed skeletonised rotor arm

sections.titleEn: To cut a long story short
sections.bodyEn: Redesigned and slimmer Light-catcher™ case. NEW mid-case for a more rugged look. NEW conical crown with crown guards. Sapphire ‘exhibition’ caseback for a view of the movement. NEW polished lacquer dial. NEW slimmer, four-faceted polished hands. Simpler seconds hand – with non-Trident counterbalance. Diamond-polished and tapered indexes – filled with lume. Bolder, fully painted GMT hand. Sellita SW330-2 movement with 56-hour power reserve. NEW in-house-designed rotor with skeletonised arm. Reproportioned, larger bezel at a shallower angle for increased legibility. ‘Sealander’ logotype on the dial for the first time. NEW 42mm size. The debut of iLink™, a system that enables tool-free link adjustment on Bader and Consort™ bracelets. Also available on sporty rubber strap with Bader buckle. Available in the NEW warmer White, NEW Pistachio, NEW Pink, Sky Blue plus Black.

Finishing the movement is a new refined, skeletonised rotor: sandblasted beneath, with raised Christopher Ward text and a debossed twin-flags logo. Linear brushing across the upper surfaces contrasts with concentric circular brushing on the rotor weight – considered detailing, executed with precision.
Re-proportioned bezel and slimmer Light-catcher™ case
New conical crown with crown guards
Linear and circular brushed skeletonised rotor arm

Sellita SW300-1 COSC Automatic Launched in 2008, Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300-1 automatic movement is one of the most respected calibres in Swiss watchmaking. At 25.6mm in diameter and with a height of 3.6 mm (one millimetre less than the SW200-1), it has a frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (4 Hz) and boasts a power reserve of 56 hours. Seen as an alternative to ETA’s 2892-A2 calibre, the SW300-1 can be customised with various complications, including date, moonphase, and GMT functions.
Crunchy, sugar-crystal dial in six high-calorie shades.
Exhibition caseback with sweet Pic ’n’ Mix printing.
Thirty-six millimetre, Grade 2 titanium case finished three ways.
Each watch is packaged with a striped Pic ’n’ Mix paper bag.

Sellita SW300 Automatic Powering the C60 Sapphire Edge is Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300 automatic movement, which boasts a power reserve of 56 hours. At 25.6mm in diameter and with a height of 3.6mm – one millimetre less than the SW200-1 – its thinner profile helped us reduce the case thickness and increase the watch’s wearability.
Sapphire The sapphire countdown bezel adds a refined sheen without compromising toughness. It’s engineered to provide the perfect ‘click’.

Housing it all is a newly developed 40.5mm Light-catcher™ case, fitted with box-domed sapphire crystals front and back. The case’s carefully balanced proportions ensure the watch sits comfortably on the wrist, while alternating brushed and polished surfaces emphasise the signature Light-catcher™ geometry. Completing the design is a newly refined Bader bracelet with polished bevels on each link, a graceful taper, and a micro-adjust clasp for travelling comfort. Or a new FKM rubber strap – snuggly integrated at the lug with a textured upper and deployant Bader buckle.
Conceived by technical director Frank Stelzer, it’s built on the foundations of Calibre CW-001 – formerly ‘Calibre SH21’ – the five-day, twin-barrelled movement we launched in 2014.

The first True GMT calibre from a British brand, CW-002 is COSC-certified and joins the small, elite circle of GMT movements. Built on CW-001, it integrates a new GMT mechanism without increasing movement height.
40.5mm Light-catcher™ case with box-domed sapphire crystals front and back, alternating brushed and polished surfaces, and balanced proportions for everyday comfort.
Diamond-polished hour, minute, and small seconds hands, all filled with Super-LumiNova® for low-light legibility; GMT hand and power-reserve indicator lacquered for contrast.

Partially open and deliberately layered, the dial prioritises local time and home time while recessing secondary indicators. Small seconds, power reserve, date, and exposed GMT bridge add depth and utility.
Rhodium-plated movement with circular Côtes de Genève, visible twin barrels and balance wheel, and a tungsten rotor with sunray-polished and sandblasted surfaces.
Applied markers, polished and faceted, filled with Super-LumiNova® for clear visibility in all conditions.

Depth by design The C1 Jump Hour Mk V has a dramatically complex four tier dial construction. At the centre sits a three-dimensional inner piece stamped with 27 concentric circles. A polished, applied circular-brushed metal ring rises above, and beyond this, a sapphire ring printed with minute markers. A sapphire minute hand with a unique stepped-design - a first for Christopher Ward. Completed by a multi-Super-LumiNova® layered undercoat, for an ethereal, cool blue glow in low light.
The four-tier dial creates extraordinary visual depth by day, and by night
Mastery of sapphire – heavily box-domed crystal, and unique design sapphire minute hand
The four-tier dial creates extraordinary visual depth by day, and by night
Dial ring and minute hand are undercoated with multiple layers of Super-LumiNova®
Detailed caseback denoting the 12-hour stops of the jump hour wheel and the minutes between
Low-light legibility in a truly original way our sapphire dial ring allows every concealed hour to charge, offering all-night time-telling

The Bel Canto Classic sits alongside the original, but brings something more complex, more traditional – more, well, classic. The box sapphire crystal delivers mid-century Italian charm, while the Roman numerals on the time-telling dial add the elegance of something that's never needed to shout. If the original Bel Canto was made for the awards ceremony, the Classic makes its mark at the invite-only aperitivo.

sections.titleEn: FS01: the mechanism behind the music
sections.bodyEn: One note. Perfected. An extrapolation of our JJ01 ‘jumping hour’ module, Calibre FS01 creates a D-note chime thanks to a U-shaped gong that doubles back on itself around the rim of the face, and a bird-shaped hammer mechanism, where the beak indicates whether the complication is on or off, and the tail strikes to make the sound.

Calibre CW-001 Our first-ever in-house movement, and an immensely stable COSC-certified calibre with a remarkable 120-hour power reserve, achieved through twin mainspring barrels. It's as handsome as it is high performance. Over a decade old, the CW-001 continues to be a reliable and much-loved calibre and proof that strength and beauty aren't mutually exclusive.
Domed sapphire crystals let you view every shining surface of CW-001.
The multi-angled bridgework is made with the Elara NS CNC milling machine.
Domed sapphire crystals let you view every shining surface of CW-001.
Lume-filled rhodium minute ring and handset deliver luminosity after dark.
The bracelet’s butterfly clasp has an adjustment mechanism – a first in The Twelve series – letting you change the length by up to 1.5mm per side - 3mm total.
The watch’s matte-black DLC coating whispers its presence.
CW-001 delivers chronometer accuracy with a five-day power reserve.

As with previous CW ‘ombré’ watches, the lacquered deep-brown dial gradually changes from light to dark toward the edge – without sacrificing legibility. The lume-filled handset delivers clarity and precision, while the ‘5N gold’ indexes – also filled with Super-LumiNova® – boast diamond-polished facets that catch the light. The date wheel at 6 o’clock is colour-matched to the dial, while the applied twin-flags logo – also in 5N gold – adds balance and depth.

Lacquered, shaded, perfected Each dial is spun at high speed during the application of paint – a process which takes the shade from light to dark as you move away from the centre. Layers of lacquer are then applied to increase its lustre.

Whichever model you choose, the perfectly chamfered hour indexes have been filled with even more Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1, while the twin-flags logo is applied – and carries a subtle brushed finish. The lume-filled handset makes telling the time a dream, while the fourth brightly-coloured GMT hand – also filled with lume – lets you monitor another time zone with accuracy, day or night.

Greenwich mean time The ‘GMT’ stands for Greenwich Mean Time – mean solar time at the Prime Meridian in Greenwich, London. It serves as a global time standard, often used to coordinate time across different regions – hence its use in aviation, and following this, as a horological complication.

Everything about the C60 Trident Pro 300 is made for daily wear: smart enough for the office, rugged enough to accompany you on the deepest of dives. Its unidirectional bezel boasts a rotating outer section with coloured ceramic insert, and a fixed steel inner ring, with minute increments all the way around.

“The new Christopher Ward C60 Trident Pro 300 collection definitely has massive appeal. This series will be perfect for people looking for an affordable dive watch that has it all, from a set of great specs and modern looks to a variety of different color and strap options. And by affordable, I mean really affordable.” – Jorg Weppelink, Author

Thanks to the genius of Calibre JJ04, our in-house modular movement, the moon is linked to the hour hand and is in constant motion, with the phases of the moon represented in a single smooth movement. If the watch is kept wound, JJ04 delivers accuracy for 128 years. And you can see the magic of mechanical watchmaking by turning the piece over and gazing through the sapphire case back at the movement.

Crazy about the details The dial is made from aventurine – a translucent glass invented on the island of Murano, Venice – infused with reflective flakes of copper oxide that resemble the night sky. The radically unadorned dial carries no markings apart from the words ‘Swiss Made’ at 6 o’clock, so you can experience both the beauty of the oversized moon, and the shimmer of aventurine as it plays with the light.

Slick, highly technical, supremely well-considered and innovative across the board, The C12 Loco is Christopher Ward at its most modern, most exciting, and most unexpected: a glittering, ever-moving, none-more-alive landmark watch to appeal to the child in each of us, yes, but to the technocrat too. As elite-level haute-horology made accessible to all, it’s one of the most explicit iterations of the Christopher Ward mission to date.

Architecture and artistry For all its intricate, whirring elegance, you never for one moment forget that The C12 Loco is a sports watch, with everything that implies: technical ability; a crisp, clean contemporary confidence. It’s nothing less than the spiritual child of Louis Cartier and Le Corbusier working in unlikely but delightful harmony…

On the C60 Trident Lumière, the chamfered indexes are made entirely from Globolight XP©, as is the unmistakable ‘twin flags’ logo and most of the handset. In all, 17 specially-shaped blocks of Globolight XP© are used on the dial which contains five times the lume of any previous Trident (and which cost four times more to produce than a ‘regular’ dial). And because the dial comes in three extraordinary colour options – and whose ‘stippled grain’ surface adds extra texture – there’ll be a shade that’s right for you.
This chronometer version has been tested by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping.

The Extreme GMT also introduces our V-Strap – our first-ever quick-release sports strap designed for serious action. Built from military-grade Cordura® in a bold two-piece construction, it features our signature 4mm taper for optimal wrist fit, a logo-etched metal fastening, and industrial-strength Velcro® that lets you strip it off in seconds. Choose black or orange. Standard or XL. Ready when you are.

At just 4.1mm thick, the SW330-2 has 25 jewels and beats at a rate of 28,800 per hour with a power reserve of up to 56 hours. The central GMT hand can be set independently from the hour and seconds hands.
41mm brushed marine-grade, steel case with Light-catcher™ design. Combined with our first ever Sandblasted bezel.
The bright orange GMT hand – painted with Super-LumiNova® – enables you to monitor any time zone around the world.
18 separate pieces of Globolight® luminous ceramic deliver maximum lume when lights are low.
Deep-stamped steel backplate features a 20th century style globe motif.
A new rubberised anti-shock holder keeps the movement secure. In case of impact, the mount absorbs and distributes energy.
Our all-new V-Strap makes its debut on the Extreme. Military-grade Cordura® construction, quick-release Velcro® closing, logo-etched hardware.

The unidirectional bezel has been industrially sandblasted, providing a textured contrast to the super-visible raised numerals, while the triangle marker is filled with Super-LumiNova® Grade X1 BL C1 to aid timing at depth. The product of extensive research, the bezel also delivers 120 clicks per rotation – providing you with tactile reassurance should you wish to use it as a diving aid.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a date wheel, a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.

sections.titleEn: A watch for the whole of your life
sections.bodyEn: The Twelve brings the pleasures of such pieces with none of the downsides. Fittingly, it’s home to some of Christopher Ward’s boldest design moves. It has a twelve-sided bezel – dodecagonal, no less – which gives a subtle scalloped look. It features a heavily textured three-dimensional dial, built of little moguls referencing the ‘pluses’ of the twin-flags logo. And it has a remarkable combination of intriguing surface finishes on case, bracelet and bezel.

Brace with impact The Twelve’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

Sellita SW200 COSC The C65 Dune Aeolian Bronze is gorgeous on the outside, but just as impressive beneath its ever-changing case, where you’ll find the strong, durable Swiss-made Sellita SW200 COSC Automatic movement, officially designated a ‘chronometer’ by the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres, and therefore amongst the most accurate mechanical movements around.

Inspired by the British Military’s quartz watches of the 1980s, the dial plays host to three subdials – controlled by pushers on the side of the case – which not only deliver a wealth of stopwatch options, but are dedicated to one of the Services through different coloured hands. And, in a first for a Military Collection, both the flat-polished numerals and logo have been applied for added depth.
Dial of delights The reverse panda dial boasts three subdials – with the hand of each one coloured to a particular Service: red for the Army; dark blue for the Navy; light blue for the RAF.

Sellita SW200 COSC Befitting a watch named for the British Army, the C65 Sandhurst is powered by extremely rugged and precise Swiss-made automatic movement - in this case, a chronometer-certified version of the Sellita SW200-1. Tested by the Controle Officiel Suisse des Chronometres, an institute responsible for ensuring the highest standards of horological excellence, the SW200-1 has been tested in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping throughout.
“Christopher Ward created their own version of the legendary military watch and made it more modern and legible.” – Marin Bilendzic

Sellita SW300-1 COSC Automatic Launched in 2008, Sellita’s 25-jewel SW300-1 automatic movement is one of the most respected calibres in Swiss watchmaking. At 25.6mm in diameter and with a height of 3.6 mm (one millimetre less than the SW200-1), it has a frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (4 Hz) and boasts a power reserve of 56 hours. Seen as an alternative to ETA’s 2892-A2 calibre, the SW300-1 can be customised with various complications, including date, moonphase, and GMT functions.

Spring into the deep The ‘compression’ spring – the width of four human hairs – is key to the mechanics of the C65 Super Compressor Elite and enables the case to become more watertight as you descend. It’s placed within the compression ring and can be seen through the caseback.

Swiss perfection Unlike some moonphase complications that transition once per day, JJ04 offers a more dynamic approach. Using the Sellita SW220 as a base, the date wheel, along with its spring-loading assembly, have been stripped out and replaced by four further wheels to drive the moon disc, with two more required for the setting mechanism.

JJ04: perpetually brilliant The C1 Moonglow is powered by CW’s own modular movement, JJ04, which is able to follow the waxing (and waning) of the moon accurately for 128 years. This also allows the watch’s ‘moons’ to chart a continuous, uninterrupted journey across the dial.

And, like so many of our watches, the story of this 41mm diameter titanium version of The Twelve owes its creation more to impassioned conversation than any masterpiece of market positioning: on this occasion the lively conversation was between Will Brackfield, our senior designer, Jorg Bader Jnr, head of product development and me as we wandered through midtown New York on our way to visit the WatchTime show in New York on a drizzly Sunday morning. The first ‘X’ prototype, which we had recently been reviewing, was a joy to behold: the most extensive open-heart surgery of our 5 day chronometer movement had achieved a view, front and back, that took our collective breaths away. But on that walk to Gotham Hall on Broadway, we wondered aloud whether by pushing the aesthetic boundaries further by reconsidering finish of the bridges and by using two grades of titanium on the case, we could elevate it to an even higher plane, and make it even more special.

Beauty and the bridges The multi-layered, multi-angled bridgework which supports the movement is only possible through the use of the Elara NS CNC milling machine, which uses a diamond cutter to achieve incredible accuracy. The work was undertaken by Paoluzzo, a maker of precision medical, aviation and horological parts.

First created near Venice some 400 years ago, aventurine is a very special sort of glass, infused with reflective copper oxide flakes. With its entire dial made of this most charismatic of materials, the new Moonphase is able to perfectly imitate the star-speckled night sky. Since each piece of aventurine is different to any other, it makes every watch unique.

Built around surely the most romantic of all watch complications, our Moonphase echoes the waxing and waning of the moon with great accuracy – and for a mighty 128 years. For all this time, your watch’s own moons will chart a graceful unbroken journey across the dial’s star-splattered night-time sky.

The strap offering is also on point. There are size different coloured solid rubber straps to choose from, so you can match or contrast with your watch depending on your mood (there’s also a bracelet option if you prefer). And because each strap and bracelet is fitted with Christopher Ward’s quick-release system, you can swap in seconds.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.

The Ti differs in other ways, too. The dial is here treated to a graduated tint, from dark charcoal at the edges to one of three exclusive colours at the centre. And inside lives a more sophisticated movement than the one in the standard steel model too. Sellita’s SW300-1 boasts chronometer certification and longer 56-hour power reserve, while its slimmer size allows for an even more wrist-hugging case. Indeed, it’s just 8.95mm tall, a full millimetre shorter than the steel version – just another remarkable stat about a remarkable watch.

Brace with impact The Twelve’s bracelet is built from single links to deliver a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm, while the satinised finish comes courtesy of a water-grinding process. The bracelet closes with a butterfly clasp – fitted with a micro-adjustment mechanism. This allows the wearer to adjust the length by up to 1.5mm per side – and 3mm in total.

Turn the watch over and a sapphire crystal, placed in the 12-sided case back, displays the elaboré-finished rotor of the Sellita SW200-1 movement. Finally, take in the elegant, integrated Twelve bracelet, whose single-link design features a taper that goes from 25mm to 17mm and a butterfly clasp for easy removal.

The 26-jewel movement boasts a date wheel, a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.
A new, polished, lacquered dial in Midnight Black, with elevated date window

sections.titleEn: A field watch made for the skies
sections.bodyEn: Sellita SW200 COSC Befitting a watch named for the Royal Air Force, the C65 Cranwell is powered by extremely rugged and precise Swiss-made automatic movement - in this case, a chronometer-certified version of the Sellita SW200-1. Tested by the Controle Officiel Suisse des Chronometres, an institute responsible for ensuring the highest standards of horological excellence, the SW200-1 has been tested in a number of positions and temperatures to ensure precision timekeeping throughout.
“Each watch in the military collection sports some of the modern design touches from Christoper Ward.” – Thomas Calara

sections.titleEn: Inspired by the brave. Engineered by the best
sections.bodyEn: Take the ultra-tough, ultra-light forged carbon dial. Made from chopped carbon fibres infused with resin (there are around 500,000 fibres per square inch), forged carbon has a uniquely unfinished look, with the dark and light greys contrasting beautifully. Around the dial is a first for Christopher Ward: a rotating inner-compass bezel which lets you orientate yourself using the sun.

The movement boasts a 4Hz frequency (equating to a smooth eight ticks per second) and a 38-hour power reserve. It also has an in-built anti-shock system to maintain accuracy when faced with any sudden jolts.

Sellita SW200-1 Automatic A workhorse watch demands a workhorse to power it, and you’ll find few hardier movements than Dune’s Sellita SW200-1 Automatic. It’s Swiss-made, self-winding, and known for accuracy, reliability and a useful 38-hour power reserve – so you can leave it on the bedside table for more than a day and it won’t need rewinding.

Founded in 2020 by Mike France, Roger Smith and Alistair Audsley, the Alliance of British Watch and Clock Makers champions the entire British watch and clockmaking ecosystem - from education to apprenticeships to global promotion. Membership has grown from a few hundred to nearly 2,000, and collaborations like this directly fund the trade body’s work. The Alliance 02 is designed not just to be collected, but to help support the industry that created it. In short: not just a pocket watch. A pocket-sized banner for British horological ingenuity - with lume.

Missed out? The good news is the next opportunity starts with membership. Alliance members get first dibs on limited editions like the Alliance 02, plus priority access to British Watchmakers' Day, a year's free subscription to Oracle Time magazine, watch discounts and honestly, the most coveted enamel pin in British watchmaking.
Exhibition caseback showcasing the CW-001 chronometer-grade movement
Floating 1.4 mm sapphire top dial featuring printed Roman numerals, paired with a five-day power reserve subdial
Brass base dial with seven layers of custom Super-LumiNova®
44mm Light-catcher™ case with oversized crown for satisfying winding
